description.narrative: SIRIUS phase II is the continuation of the SIRIUS phase I, therefore the specific outcome would be very similar. The SIRIUS project aims at continuing being an acknowledged Centre of Reference within the EU for knowledge on Digital Cross Border Investigations, and in particular on:a)formal processes (i.e. MLA Treaties between the EU and third countries);b)voluntary cooperation (i.e. direct requests originating in the EU directly submitted to foreignbased OSPs);c)Legislative developments (i.e. EU eevidence legislation).Another important change from phase I is the enhanced cooperation with OSPs by engaging with small and mediumsize OSPs based in third countries, apart from the US. Expanding geographical scope and involving small and mediumsized companies would significantly contribute to becoming a Centre of Reference for knowledge by adding on information about access to electronic evidence regardless the size and location of a company. This would ultimately lead to improved efficiency of submitting and processing data requests.Moreover, the phase II adds on a strong judicial component to the project. Stronger engagement of judicial authorities into the project would create a common knowledgesharing platform and resourcerepository for better understanding the complex and fragmented legal landscape that applies to crossborder acquisition of electronic evidence. This will ultimately improve the knowledge and practices for the usage of legal instruments to request electronic data.

title.narrative: Contribute to the development of a secure, rightsbased international digital sphere, conducive to a level playing field in terms of market access and business opportunities for EU companies.

description.narrative: The SIRIUS phase II represents the continuation and enhancement of the SIRIUS phase I, aiming at further strengthening cooperation between the Law Enforcement and Judicial Authorities and Online Service Providers. In its Second Phase, SIRIUS also intends to expand its geographical scope to include third countries, other than US, based on the interest of law enforcement and judicial authorities of EU MS. This will be done in close collaboration with existing initiatives and projects working on the selected countries, and will allow SIRIUS to remain relevant in the fast evolving landscape of digital companies.By improving cooperation between EU law enforcement, judicial authorities and foreignbased OSPs, SIRIUS project is aiming at contributing to developing a secure, rightsbased digital sphere. In doing so, SIRIUS project will intend to contribute to ensuring effective investigation and prosecution of crimes in the EU by improving the knowledge on crossborder access to electronic evidence (i.e. by improving the quality of requests). This will be done through stronger collaboration between OSPs and law enforcement and judicial authorities. It will ultimately lead to improving the speed and success rate of answers to the requests for data.
